title: Uganda Confirms 3 More Cases — Total 5 Imported Ebola Cases in Kampala
detail: Uganda confirmed three additional cases of Bundibugyo virus disease, bringing the country's total to five. The new cases included: (1) a driver who transported Uganda's first confirmed patient; (2) a health worker at a Kampala hospital who treated an infected patient; and (3) a woman from DRC who entered Uganda with mild symptoms, traveled from Arua to Entebbe, sought care at a private hospital in Kampala, initially improved and returned to DRC, then tested positive after a follow-up prompted by a tip from a pilot who had transported her. All five Ugandan cases were imported with epidemiological links traceable to DRC. No local transmission among contacts of confirmed cases had been documented in Uganda. Contact tracing teams were following 87 contacts of the first two confirmed cases.

title: US Reroutes Passengers from DRC, Uganda, South Sudan to 3 Airports for Ebola Screening
detail: The US government announced that passengers arriving from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan would be rerouted through three designated US airports — Washington Dulles (Virginia), Dallas-Fort Worth (Texas), and Atlanta (Georgia) — for enhanced Ebola screening. The measure echoed protocols used during the 2014 West Africa epidemic, when a similar funneling system was established. The three airports have specialized public health screening capacity and quarantine facilities. US Embassy Nigeria and other US embassies in Africa simultaneously updated their worldwide caution notices with Ebola-specific health screening requirements.
